# A module zip carries no generated file. So a dependency that generates part
# of its own API ships a package the compiler reads as empty, and the consumer
# fails on a symbol the dependency's source never declares. cmd/go runs that
# dependency's own directives first.

env GOFLAGS=-mod=mod

# The zip does not carry what the directive writes, so the fetch runs it. The
# extracted module is the module completed: the zip's files and the ones its own
# generators added.
go mod download example.com/generated
exists $GOPATH/pkg/mod/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go

# The build reads the completed module rather than the empty package.
go build ./...

# The directory's own checksum is recorded when it is completed, and that is
# what go mod verify holds it to. It is not the zip's checksum, and nothing is
# excluded from either of them.
exists $GOPATH/pkg/mod/cache/download/example.com/generated/@v/v1.0.0.complete
go mod verify

# A file the zip carries keeps the zip's bytes, whatever the generator wrote
# over it. What the module's authors published is the module.
grep 'the module published this' $GOPATH/pkg/mod/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/kept.go

# No setting turns this off. A fresh module cache completes the module again,
# and the symbol the generator writes is there.
env GOGENERATEDEPS=off
env GOMODCACHE=$WORK/mod-again
go build ./...
exists $WORK/mod-again/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go

-- go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.16

require example.com/generated v1.0.0
-- use.go --
package use

import "example.com/generated/lang"

var Name = lang.Name()
